propositions: Pandoc subprocess invocations can hang indefinitely (13.5 min observed hang at 95.8% CPU) because pypandoc provides no timeout and subprocess.run(timeout=) reaps only the direct child, leaving spinning grandchildren orphaned.

The renderer must replace subprocess.run with caller-side Popen(start_new_session=True) + communicate(input=unit, timeout=dc_pandoc_timeout_s) and reap the whole process group on TimeoutExpired via rebar._proc.reap_process_group to kill CPU-spinning children.
A configurable timeout reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s (default 10s) must be wired across config schema, sources, and documentation without changing per-unit fallback semantics or rendered output.

The pypandoc-binary wheel (bundled pandoc 3.6.1, GPL) must be pinned in pyproject.toml and verified in CI; a new repo-root NOTICE file must record pandoc's GPL entry, name, version, and how it reaches installations.
Rendered output across the committed 178-body corpus (880+ units) must be byte-identical to the pre-hardening renderer, proving this change addresses robustness and not rendering semantics.

Safe-run batching optimization (46% of runs are single-unit, changes output on ~12% of bodies for ~12% spawn reduction) is descoped; the spawn tax is addressed instead by the change-gated rich_sha skip in the cutover story.
